day.text: Checking the rules: an Owl lays an egg in the visited nest when nobody else visited them. So Casey's report fits my Falcon read, and Casey is more credible than I was treating them. day.note: Casey's Owl explanation is consistent with my Falcon report and the rules: the Owl gives Drew an egg when no one else visited. So Casey now looks more credible, and the real conflict is Drew versus Finley.

day.text: Drew, my nest didn't change, so you didn't visit me. Casey's Owl story holds, so Drew is the liar. Calling CAW.
day.note: Drew's claimed Turkey visit is impossible given my dawn report, so Drew is my pick. I'll restate that and call for the vote.

day.text: Finley, a Turkey's own nest doesn't change when visited, since the visitor gets the egg. So 'my nest changed nothing' doesn't prove Drew lied. Drew, you still haven't said what you gained from Finley.
day.note: Finley's logic is wrong: a Turkey's own nest doesn't change when visited, so 'nothing changed' proves nothing. Say that and keep the Drew question open.

day.text: My Owl report is fixed: one egg for Drew from me. Drew's remaining egg would have to come from Finley the Turkey, but Finley's nest didn't change and Finley says no visit. Drew, if you're lying about visiting Finley, I'm pointing at you.
day.note: Drew's Turkey story conflicts with Finley's unchanged nest, and my Owl report stands. I'll point at Drew as the likely liar without calling an early vote.

day.text: Finley, a Turkey's nest doesn't change when visited, so "my nest didn't change" proves nothing. Your only real claim is "nobody visited me," and Drew says they did. Drew, what did you gain from Finley? Finley, what did you claim as a Turkey, and is that where your denial comes from?
day.note: Finley's nest-based argument is invalid: a Turkey's own nest never changes from visits. Finley's denial of Drew's visit is the claim to test, so I'll say that and not call for a vote yet.

day.text: I'm pointing at Finley. Finley has claimed Owl, Eagle, then Turkey, and denies the visit Drew's +2 implies.
day.note: Finley has changed roles three times this game and denies a visit that Drew's +2 supports. I'm pointing at Finley rather than Casey, who now has a consistent Owl story.

day.text: Yes, I visited Finley and my nest gained 2 from that visit. Finley says nobody came, but Finley is the Turkey, so Finley is the one who has to explain the denial. I'm pointing at Finley.
day.note: Under pressure as Meowfia. I'll stick to the visit to Finley and keep pressing Finley's denial, pointing at Finley for the trial.

Alex.note: As Falcon I learn who my target visited. Casey was Meowfia last round and leads on points, so I'll check Casey.

Blair.note: I'm the Kookaburra again and want a role check. Alex has given the most contradictory claims, so I'll visit Alex.

Casey.note: I'm Farm this round as the Owl. Casey is first at 15 and I'm not the leader, so I'll visit Drew to learn what animals came to them.

Drew.note: As Meowfia Sphinx, I learn the farm roles are Falcon, Hawk, Kookaburra, Owl, Turkey. I'll pick Turkey, since it's a stay-home role and the visit should be safe to find who it is.

Ellis.note: Hawk visit. Casey claimed Meowfia earlier, so visiting Casey may gain an egg if they're Meowfia.

audit: Casey lays 1 egg in Drew's nest
Finley lays 1 egg in Drew's nest

Alex.feeling: Tense and muddled: the claims keep contradicting each other, and the Drew-Finley visit dispute is the only thing anyone can really check.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 is messy: the Drew and Finley visit claims conflict, and Casey's Owl story has become more consistent than I first thought.

Casey.feeling: Tense and contradictory: the Owl, Turkey, and Falcon claims don't reconcile, and I'm leaning on Drew as the likely liar.

Drew.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Falcon, Owl, and Turkey stories keep colliding, and I'm the one with the most at stake.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 is messy: the nest-change claims contradict each other, and I'm not sure who is lying about the Drew and Finley visit.

Finley.feeling: Drew's claimed visit contradicts my dawn report, so I'm fairly sure Drew is lying, but the table is split and the vote is uncertain.

defence.Finley: I'm Farm, the Turkey. I was wrong to deny Drew's visit: a Turkey's nest doesn't change when visited, and I don't learn who came, so my "nobody visited me" proves nothing. Drew's +2 fits a visit to me plus Casey's Owl visit. I'm not Meowfia, so vote on the stories, not on my denial.
defence.Drew: I visited Finley and gained 2, which is the only fact I'll stand on. Finley admits the denial was wrong, and Casey's Owl story conflicts with Alex's Falcon. Vote on those, not on who pointed first.

Alex.note: Finley first denied a visit then admitted it, and changed roles several times. Drew's visit is now confirmed by Finley, so Finley is the suspicious one. Vote Finley with a few low cards.

Blair.note: Finley's shifting roles and the false denial make Finley the likelier Meowfia. I'm throwing S6 at Finley.

Casey.note: I'm Farm and Drew's visit story conflicts with the Turkey's unchanged nest. I'll throw two cards at Drew to push for their eggsecution.

Drew.note: Finley is Farm, so eliminating Finley helps Meowfia. Throwing at Finley with two wilds and the 5, keeping the 6, 8 and 12.

Ellis.note: Finley's denial was false and the Turkey story is shaky. Throw two cards at Finley.

Finley.note: I know I'm Farm, so I'm voting for Drew, the other player on trial. I'll throw H6 and S7 to keep my 8s and the 13.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visit-egg rules were hard to track, and I misread the Turkey's payout (I first said the Turkey's own nest should change, then reversed it). Confused reports made it hard to tell who was lying.
Alex.fun: Round 1 went well: Casey openly claimed Meowfia and the table converged on them, and my Eagle count matched the visit record. Watching the Owl and Turkey stories collide in round 3 was also entertaining.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can cross-check claims without guessing at egg-payment rules.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw at Finley, a Farm Turkey, on shifting role claims. Drew was the Meowfia Sphinx, so I should have thrown my high cards at Drew once Drew's +2 and visit story conflicted with Finley's denial.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were argued wrongly by several players, me included, and a confused dawn report made my own claims unreliable. Round 2's +3 and Alex's Turkey claim never got settled.
Blair.fun: Casey openly claimed Meowfia in round 1 and then still rode the Farm win, which made the table argue about the story rather than the claim. The trials were tense, with each side pushing a different suspect.
Blair.change: I'd make a confused report say plainly which part is wrong, so confused players can still help the table reason from the rest of their report.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I backed the push against Finley and threw my S6 at them, but Finley was Farm and Drew, the Sphinx, was the real Meowfia. I'd have questioned Drew's +2 claim harder and not joined the push on Finley.

Casey.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg rules were the hardest to track, since who pays whom changed how the nest counts read. I also couldn't tell from the dawn reports alone whether a nest change came from a visit or from the animal's own ability.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Blair's Kookaburra story kept shifting from Kookaburra to Hawk to confused, and the table turned on Blair. Our Meowfia side won that round without anyone knowing I was one of them.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports show who visited you when the animal's ability depends on visitors, so players aren't left reconstructing egg counts from contradictory claims.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I openly claimed Floofer and pushed the vote onto Alex, which drew the table's attention to me. Next time I would stay quiet and let the Eagle and Owl contradictions do the work.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were easy to misread: several of us got the direction of the egg payments backwards during the day, which made claims look false when they weren't.
Drew.fun: Round 1's trial, where Alex's Eagle count clashed with Finley's Owl report and the table had to untangle who was lying from the numbers alone.
Drew.change: I'd add a short reference card for how the Turkey, Owl and Eagle pay eggs, so the table can check claims without arguing over the rules.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw three cards at Blair, who was Farm, while Casey had openly claimed Meowfia; I should have thrown at Casey, since that would have won the round for us.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg rules were easy to get backwards at the table. Several of us, me included, misread who pays whom, which made the visit claims hard to check.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 was fun: Casey openly claimed Floofer and Meowfia, and the table tried to work out whether Alex's Eagle count or Finley's Owl report was the lie.
Ellis.change: I would make it clearer which animal pays the visitor and which pays the visited player, since that one rule decided most of the arguments.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I helped put Blair on trial, though Blair was Farm and Casey, the Meowfia, was the one with the contradictory Floofer-visit story. I should have pressed Casey harder, and in round 3 I threw at Finley, a Farm Turkey, when Drew was the Sphinx and Meowfia.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey rule was the one I got wrong: I assumed a visited Turkey's nest would change, but the visitor gets the egg, so my "nobody visited me" proved nothing. The two-step vote and throw counts also made it hard to read who was really trying to win.
Finley.fun: Casey openly claimed Meowfia in round 1, and the table still voted it out after the Owl and Eagle reports lined up against Alex's count. The back-and-forth over whose visit gave whose eggs was a fun puzzle.
Finley.change: I would make the dawn reports say explicitly which role and visit caused each egg change, so players can check Turkey, Owl, and Eagle claims without guessing.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I flatly declared Drew a liar based on my unchanged nest, when I should have said only what I knew and asked for the visit details. That mistake put me on trial and helped Finley's team lose the round.

review.title: The Floofer Confession
review.headline: Casey confessed Meowfia twice, survived once, and won the whole game.
review.summary: Round 1 was a Farm win after Casey, the Floofer, openly claimed Meowfia. In round 2 Casey claimed it again and still lived, because Blair, a confused Kookaburra, looked worse and the table threw at Blair. In round 3 Drew, a lone Sphinx, bluffed a visit to the Turkey and got Farm to eggsecute the real Turkey, Finley. Casey won with 16 points, mostly from one 14-point banked throw in round 2.

rounds.recap: Casey, the Floofer, admitted Meowfia on day one, and Finley's Owl report matched. Alex's Eagle report was oddly worded and drew some suspicion, but the table still voted Casey. Casey threw four cards at Alex and lost. Farm banked points and Ellis led with 13.

Casey claimed Floofer again, but Blair, a confused Kookaburra, got an unexplained +3 and a shaky story. The table argued about Turkey rules and retracted its first attack, but still threw at Blair. Blair was Farm, so Casey banked 14 and took the lead.

Drew, a lone Sphinx, claimed to have visited Finley's Turkey for +2. Finley denied any visit, but the Turkey's own nest never changes, so the denial proved nothing. Finley's earlier shifting claims were mostly the Round 2 Eagle, so the Blair read was shaky, but Finley was eggsecuted. Drew won 5 points.

highlights.text: Casey claimed Floofer and Meowfia on day one, and Finley's Owl report backed it up.
Casey threw S10, D3 and S1 at Farm Blair and banked 14 while claiming Meowfia in the open.
Drew and Ellis spotted their own Turkey mistake and retracted, which paused a Blair pile-on.
Drew's invented visit to the Turkey was nearly true to the rules, and the real Turkey was eggsecuted for denying it.

confusions.what: As Eagle, said Casey and Finley visited Blair and called Finley a liar. The Owl report said Eagle and Floofer, which Alex then misread as Finley lying.
Claimed Turkey's +0 proved nobody visited, but a Turkey pays its visitors, not itself.
Made the same Turkey error, then corrected it.
Backed the Turkey argument against Blair, then withdrew it.
As Owl, said her visit laid an egg in Drew's nest, then that Drew's visit to Finley added one more. The Owl rule did allow the first part, but her wording swung between versions.
As Turkey, argued his unchanged nest proved nobody visited him, when a Turkey's own nest never changes.
Said Finley claimed Owl, Eagle, then Turkey. Those were Finley's roles in different rounds, not shifting claims.
Reported Casey and Finley both laying eggs in Drew's nest, but Alex's Falcon rule and the Owl report were read as contradictory when they were not.
Said Casey told two stories, Drew then Finley, though she was describing Drew's own visit.

worked: Turkey and Kookaburra created real puzzles: Turkey pays visitors, and a confused report makes honest claims look like lies.
Open Meowfia claims (Floofer) forced a real tension between telling the truth and surviving.
Egg-count cross-checks gave players hard facts, such as Drew's +2 in round 3.
The consolation return and banked-throw scoring made Casey's round 2 throw a real risk and reward.
problems: Turkey's text is easy to misread: three players got it wrong in round 2 and Finley again in round 3. Add an example line saying the visitor gets the egg and the Turkey's nest is unchanged.

Confused Kookaburra gave the Meowfia a free win, since Blair could not prove a wrong report and was eggsecuted. Consider a clearer confusion tell, or let Kookaburra's confusion show on others' reports.
Floofer's open claims never cost Casey anything: round 2 had no Farm checks and the table threw at Blair. Meowfia confessing and still winning suggests Farm lacks a way to verify claims.
Round 3 was decided by unverifiable visit claims, because a lone Meowfia can invent a Turkey visit that Farm cannot disprove. Consider announcing visit counts or giving Turkey a notification.
Round 2 had one Meowfia and scores swung 14 points on one throw, so the leader decides the game. Consider capping banked values or catch-up rules.
